problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=⟨1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=6t.$ Find $R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$

feedback.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s={e}^{t}-1.$ Given that $R(s)$ is the parametrization of the given curve by its arc length $s,$ what is the $x$-component of $R?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, since $s={e}^{t}-1,$ we have that $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1).$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s,$ with $s\ge 0,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)}\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)}\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(s+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(s+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, the $x$-component of $R$ is

$$
\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(s+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)].
$$
